india.label: Diplomacy · 16 Nov
india.headline: Modi heads to Manila for the ASEAN and East Asia summits
india.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi left for Manila ahead of the ASEAN–India and East Asia summits on 17 November. He put trade, connectivity and maritime security among India’s priorities.
india.context: Watch for concrete commitments on trade and transport links in the summit statements.

india.label: Weather · 16 Nov
india.headline: IMD expects the Bay of Bengal depression to strengthen
india.summary: In its Monday morning outlook, the IMD forecast that the deep depression could become Cyclone Akvan by evening and strengthen further on 17 November.
india.context: The track and intensity can change as the system develops. For coastal travel, check the latest IMD bulletin and district advisories.

india.label: Climate innovation · 16 Nov
india.headline: The Earthshot Prize brings William and Kate to Mumbai
india.summary: Prince William and Catherine arrived in Mumbai on Monday for a three-day visit centred on the Earthshot Prize, which recognises environmental solutions.
india.context: The awards offer a shortlist of projects to follow. Look for evidence that the winning ideas can work at a larger scale.

india.label: Trade · 15 Nov
india.headline: Goyal says India and the US agreed on preferential access
india.summary: Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal said on Sunday that the US had agreed to give Indian goods preferential access relative to competing suppliers. He did not specify product-level rates or an implementation date.
india.context: The commercial effect will depend on the covered products, tariff schedules and effective dates.

india.label: Delhi · 16 Nov
india.headline: Chhath and the trade fair bring Delhi traffic changes
india.summary: Delhi Traffic Police advised commuters to avoid affected roads around Bharat Mandapam during the trade fair and announced Chhath restrictions near five Yamuna ghats.
india.context: The two events affect different parts of Delhi. Check the route-specific advisory before travelling.

world.label: Southeast Asia · 16 Nov
world.headline: ASEAN opens its Manila summit
world.summary: Southeast Asian leaders opened their annual summit with the economic fallout from global conflicts, Myanmar and tensions in the South China Sea on the agenda.
world.context: The final communiqué will show how far members agree on maritime rules and engagement with Myanmar.

world.label: Red Sea · 15 Nov
world.headline: Yemeni government forces pull back from a key strait
world.summary: Yemeni government forces announced a withdrawal from the area around Bab el-Mandeb to focus on defending Aden, Reuters reported.
world.context: The strait connects the Red Sea with the Gulf of Aden. Shipping notices and rerouting decisions will show how operators assess the change.

world.label: Peru · 15 Nov
world.headline: Pope Leo calls for protection of the Amazon and its defenders
world.summary: Speaking to a largely Indigenous audience in Peru, Pope Leo condemned deforestation and pollution associated with gold and oil production and called for killings of Indigenous leaders to be investigated.
world.context: The speech puts enforcement against illegal extraction and protection for local communities in the same frame.

world.label: Cabo Verde · 15 Nov
world.headline: Jobs and emigration shape Cabo Verde’s presidential vote
world.summary: Cabo Verde voted on Sunday, with incumbent José Maria Neves facing a former justice minister who became the country’s first woman to run for president, Reuters reported.
world.context: Youth employment was central to the campaign. The island nation’s large diaspora makes emigration a domestic political issue as well.

world.label: Thailand · 16 Nov
world.headline: Early-morning fire kills 11 in Phuket
world.summary: Thai police told Reuters that a fire in a Phuket commercial shophouse killed 11 people and injured 16 early Monday.
world.context: The police count is an early report. The cause and circumstances still require investigation.

markets.label: Index snapshot · 9:21 a.m. IST
markets.headline: Nifty and Sensex rebound after Friday’s decline
markets.summary: On 16 November at 9:21 a.m. IST, Nifty 50 was up 0.45% at 25,256 and Sensex was up 0.56% at 82,030.41. Friday’s cash session closed lower before the weekend break.
markets.context: Reuters linked the stronger open to foreign inflows and softer crude. These are intraday levels.

markets.label: Sector movers · 16 Nov open
markets.headline: IT heavyweights help lift the opening tape
markets.summary: At the open, The Financial Express reported TCS up 1.56%, Infosys up 1.32% and HCL Technologies up 1.24%. Asian Paints and Bharti Airtel also advanced.
markets.context: The gains in heavyweight names help explain the higher benchmark. Watch whether the rally broadens beyond those stocks.

markets.label: Company catalyst · 16 Nov morning
markets.headline: Tata Motors PV falls as JLR cuts its outlook
markets.summary: Reuters reported Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles down 7.5% at ₹265.90 in its morning update. JLR cut its fiscal-year core earnings margin outlook from 4% to 2–3%.
markets.context: The revised JLR cash-outflow estimate of about £1.25 billion puts cash generation alongside margin recovery on the watch list.

markets.label: IPO calendar · 16 Nov, 8:16 a.m. IST
markets.headline: Three issues are scheduled to open this week
markets.summary: Crystal Crop Protection bidding is scheduled for 18–20 November. Mahanadi Coalfields and SME issuer Watrana Rentals are due to open on 19 November. Upstox listed no IPO debut this week.
markets.context: Crystal Crop’s indicated band is ₹259–272 and Mahanadi’s is ₹129–136. Check the exchange timetable and offer documents for any changes.

markets.label: Commodities · 16 Nov morning
markets.headline: Brent eases and indicative Indian gold is ₹1,37,610
markets.summary: The Financial Express quoted Brent at $95.52 a barrel, down 0.33%, and reported an indicative Indian 24-carat gold price of ₹1,37,610 per 10 grams.
markets.context: Compare gold quotes by purity, city and timestamp. For oil, track whether the early move lasts through the Indian session.

tech.label: US industrial policy · 16 Nov
tech.headline: US AI ‘national champions’ plan reported
tech.summary: Reuters relayed a Wall Street Journal report that the US administration plans to designate more than two dozen AI firms, including Nvidia, Microsoft, OpenAI and Anthropic, to help them expand overseas.
tech.context: Reuters had yet to independently confirm the report. An official announcement would clarify eligibility and the form of support.

tech.label: Semiconductors · 16 Nov
tech.headline: SK Hynix plans five years of supplier support
tech.summary: SK Hynix said it plans to spend ₩1.4 trillion, about $1.05 billion, over five years to support South Korean suppliers of semiconductor materials, parts and equipment.
tech.context: The investment highlights the importance of upstream suppliers when memory makers scale production for AI hardware.

tech.label: Assessment · 15 Nov
tech.headline: South Korea’s top tax-exam scorer admits using AI to cheat
tech.summary: The candidate said he photographed questions with a small camera, sent them to a generative AI tool and checked responses on a smartphone.
tech.context: The case shows how small devices can bring outside assistance into a supervised exam room.

tech.label: AI education · 16 Nov
tech.headline: China pushes for AI literacy in schools by 2030
tech.summary: Reuters reported on China’s drive toward universal AI literacy by 2030, including a Beijing school where students use AI to build apps and program robots.
tech.context: That private school illustrates one approach. Learning outcomes across ordinary classrooms and different age groups will be more informative.

tech.label: AI business · 16 Nov
tech.headline: Nvidia earnings and Anthropic’s listing test AI sentiment
tech.summary: Reuters reported that Asian shares slipped on Monday as investors awaited Nvidia earnings on 17 November and the scheduled start of Anthropic trading on 19 November.
tech.context: Nvidia’s outlook offers evidence on chip demand. The listing shows how public investors value a major model developer.

mind.label: Decision psychology · 2015
mind.headline: Fear and anger can pull risk judgments in different directions
mind.summary: A behavioural-science review describes experiments in which fear raised perceived risk and anger lowered it, including for events unrelated to the cause of the emotion.
mind.context: Before a consequential decision, name the emotion you are carrying and ask whether it comes from the decision itself. That can help you check your first impression.
mind.source: Lerner et al., Annual Review of Psychology

mind.label: Group behaviour · 2010
mind.headline: Turn-taking is one clue to how well groups work
mind.summary: In experiments with 699 people, group performance across tasks was associated with more equal conversational turn-taking and higher social sensitivity.
mind.context: In a meeting, try a short first round so quieter participants can contribute before discussion settles around the first idea. The experiment found associations.

mind.label: Work psychology · 2026
mind.headline: Unfinished tasks can follow you after hours
mind.summary: A meta-analysis found that unfinished work was associated with more work-related thoughts during off-hours. The associations were strongest for emotionally charged rumination.
mind.context: Try leaving a written next action before signing off. The analysis measured the association with unfinished tasks, and the note is a practical experiment to try.
mind.source: Wendsche et al., Anxiety, Stress & Coping

mind.label: Evolution · 2022
mind.headline: Guppies can evolve similar traits through many small genetic effects
mind.summary: Trinidadian guppies repeatedly evolved similar life-history traits across predation environments. Genetic mapping suggested many small effects for traits such as male age and size at maturity.
mind.context: Similar outcomes can emerge through a complex genetic basis. The visible trait gives only part of the evolutionary story.

mind.label: Evolution · 2018
mind.headline: Hurricanes can change which lizards survive
mind.summary: After two hurricanes, researchers revisiting island anoles found that survivors differed from the pre-storm populations in body size, limb proportions and toe-pad size.
mind.context: A single extreme event can impose strong selection. Following later generations would show whether the population shift persists.

marketing.label: India · MakeMyTrip · 14 Nov
marketing.headline: MakeMyTrip gives a travel sale a familiar ritual
marketing.summary: The India-focused Travel Ka Muhurat Sale launched with six films starring Alia Bhatt and Ranveer Singh, covering flights, stays and other categories. Members had early access and limited offers ran in evening windows.
marketing.context: A culturally familiar moment can coordinate attention. Separate creative by shopping need, and make the actual offer windows easy to find.

marketing.label: India · Google Android · 10 Nov
marketing.headline: A day without an itinerary becomes an Android demo
marketing.summary: Google India followed Kareena Kapoor Khan around Singapore in a film released on Instagram and YouTube, using tasks such as identifying Peranakan shophouses to show Gemini in use.
marketing.context: Build a demo around moments where a feature answers a question the audience can immediately understand.

marketing.label: India · CP PLUS · 5 Nov
marketing.headline: CP PLUS uses a familiar phrase to introduce smarter security
marketing.summary: CP PLUS featured Ranveer Singh in a new Indian brand film that revisits its familiar Hindi surveillance line while introducing AI-powered security features.
marketing.context: A recognisable line can carry existing brand recognition into a new product story. Show clearly what the added capability does.

marketing.label: Global · Deutsche Telekom · 2 Nov
marketing.headline: Deutsche Telekom produces one festive story for ten markets
marketing.summary: Take Time to Connect launched in Slovakia and was planned for ten European markets. It tells a grandfather–granddaughter story, with cuts ranging from six seconds to 140 seconds for different placements.
marketing.context: Decide which moment conveys the story on its own before planning shorter edits. Keep the idea recognisable across placements.

marketing.label: Global · Tesco UK · 1 Nov
marketing.headline: Tesco makes grocery delivery central to a Christmas film
marketing.summary: The Wrong Address reunites two former school friends after a misdirected grocery order. Tesco debuted a 60-second version on ITV and extended the campaign with social content and in-store experiences.
marketing.context: A service can do the dramatic work in a story. Here delivery creates the problem, gives the characters a reason to meet and carries the brand’s message.
